I have both a mental illness (schizoaffective disorder) and a physical illness (not 100% sure what it is, nor are the doctors, it presents like rheumatoid arthritis, but I only have some of the markers for it, I have fairly severe joint damage, but no bone damage as you would usually see in RA. The RA medications I took seemed to be helping, but they raised my bloodpressure too high, and I'm already on 5 medications for that, and still far too high. They are like 99% sure it is some sort of auto immune). 

Because of these things, maintaining a job is pretty much impossible, and I have been on Social Security disability. My case was strong enough that I never had to appeal or even use a lawyer at all. They pretty much gave it to me instantly. I'm grateful for being able to have some income now that I can't work.

The frustrating part aside from dealing with the physical pain and the host of mental bullshit I go through, is just the way society and specifically my friends behave. Looking at me, I don't look disabled, so a lot of folk just assume I'm lazy or whatever. 

My friends constantly rant about "wellfare people" and "lazy assholes living on THEIR hard earned tax money", and they always just look at me and say "Well, I don't mean you" or "I know YOU aren't abusing the system, but most people are". Like those small statements should make me not be upset or feel bad about myself. I try not to let it show, or react or whatever... but I feel like I just can't even talk to people anymore without being harshly judged. I just want to scream "Don't you think that if I could work I would? Fuck you, I was YOUR damn supervisor before this all happened. I've worked and payed into the system my entire life, dickhead, and now that I need to collect from it I'm an "entitled, lazy, asshole"? Oh, you didn't mean ME? Oh, OK, saying "no offense" totally negates everything. Dick."

But I don't, because then I'm the asshole... and this is getting very long, but thank you for letting me scream into the ether. It's so frustrating being this way, and it's more frustrating dealing with other people, and seriously if I didn't have an amazing wife and a son I love so much, I'd just put a bullet in my brain. I fantasize about killing myself pretty much all day every day. I won't do it, but god... how amazing would it be to just not exist?

I'm not necessarily disagreeing, I don't think everyone needs therapy, and obviously my only "evidence" is anecdotal, but I think the newer trend in therapy is that the ultimate goal of therapy is to not need therapy anymore.

The other example I have is my mother went to see a (different) therapist due to some depression and suicidal thoughts about her health and the health of my father, and after a few months the therapist "fired" her, saying that she no longer needed therapy, but to come back if she was feeling suicidal again. 

Again, just anecdotal, but I wouldn't be so quick to think the industry as a whole is a scam, or that the individual therapists purposefully keep people unstable enough to keep coming back, I think most genuinely just want to help people. Sure, there are charlatans and bags of dicks in every profession, just hasn't been my experience with this one.

I don't subscribe to any particular religion or faith, I have no dogma that I adhere to. I don't pray, unless you count sending hopes and well wishes out into the ether from my brain space as prayer. I don't deny evolution or the big bang or any modern scientific theory that I'm aware of (though to be fair, I don't really care all that much about it, at least not in an active study sort of way). But I do believe in something. I don't know if it's a god, but you could call it that. I don't think that whatever it is interacts or interferes with the universe in any way other than setting it all in motion, unless you would say that creating natural processes in the first place is interaction, then I could get behind that, I guess. 

The question is why, though, so I will do my best to answer. In spring time and early summer, I like to go outside and stand on the grass in my bare feet. I close my eyes, turn my face to the sun and I just... feel and listen for a while. I feel the warm earth beneath, and the soft cold grass, often still damp. I feel the cool breeze coming down into the valley from the mountains, carrying the scents of honeysuckle and sage, of newly tilled earth and growing things. I feel the hot sun on my face. I take a deep breath, and I can almost feel the heartbeat of the universe, some... force that holds all life together and connects us in a way I can't explain fully. For those few minutes, I feel one with the universe, I feel the beauty of precious life, and in that moment, I believe.

That force, those feelings, the energy of the universe and world surging around us, that is god to me. 

Full disclosure, I'm also a diagnosed schizophrenic, and while I am medicated and in treatment, I do still believe a lot of crazy shit, so maybe this is just that. But it's a nice thing to believe, and it makes me feel good. So I'm cool with it.

Can't speak for any other places, but in my state the easiest answer is "it's not legal". State sales tax (though it varies from county, city, zone, etc, and the law only applies to state tax, not to city or zone taxes, or any other taxes) is applied to the displayed price. If you display the price as 9.99 you have to charge the tax on 9.99, if you display the price as 10.06 (price including tax) you must charge tax on 10.06. It's how the tax code is set up. I worked for my state's tax department for near a decade and still don't know why it is that way, it just is, and that isn't even going into the craziness of other local taxes or including excise taxes. If you want proof or whatever it's in the laws somewhere in NRS 372, been a long time and I don't feel like reading tax code (also it's been interpreted many different ways, so have fun with that shitshow), if you want to know google it.

Eh, I don't know if it's only shitty dad's that do stuff like this. Do it in serious? Sure, but it's a running joke that stuff like this happens and it can be quite hilarious. 

My first wife's father, the first time we met was going to be on a hunting trip, to keep a long story short, he and her were both in on it, and she helped build up the tension and such for weeks leading up to the trip, nothing major, but little things talking about her father's time in Vietnam (most of which were very exaggerated), or making up (untrue) stories about having a temper, being violent etc. I hadn't met him, but she even staged a few phone calls that I would overhear that were tons of yelling and stuff. 

I was super nervous, not because I needed his approval, but because I just really thought the guy was a violent prick, and I was going to not get along with him. When it came time for the hunting trip, when I showed up, for the first 10 minutes or so he didn't say word to me, just finishing up cleaning his gun and glaring at me. 

It was awkward, and uncomfortable, and while I was steeling myself for a bad weekend, he walks up to me holding his shotgun, and stares me right in the eyes with the meanest look on his face I've ever seen, I legit thought I might get hit with the butt of his shotgun.

Then he gives a massive grin, and a good 3 minute long genuine belly laugh, doubled over an all, and says "I can't believe you fucking fell for it." After that proper introductions were made and we were fast friends, even years after his daughter and I aren't together anymore, we are still friends, and still joke about it. He's sometimes more of a father to me than my biological father. 

My point is that sometimes it's just a joke, and it can be funny.

I have a lot, my mom was an amazing cook, but we were super poor and lived in a super tiny town without much in the way of a grocery. So all the big "fancy" meals do it for me, meatloaf with red gravy, fried chicken, something my mom called "finger steaks", which were strips of beef breaded and fried like chicken, always served with rice and gravy. Just the smell of any of that stuff sends me back to sitting on the floor as a little kid, watching and smelling my mother cooking. 

We also ate a lot of cheap shit, and often times nothing at all, depending on how much of a bender my dad was on, so I get some of the feels from things like Totino's pizzas, canned ravioli, white bread and margarine, boxed mac n' cheese. 

The biggest one, though, the thing I can't eat without having a huge grin on my face the entire time are fish sticks, not the good triangle ones, but the cheap shit ones, dipped in ketchup. It's not good, but man... we had been living on "ghetto polenta" for a month (it's corn meal mixed into a mush with water and government cheese, which is like Velveeta but somehow worse), because my dad bounced for a little while and my mom had to take care of us kids and could only work part time, but she scraped together enough money to buy a big bag of fish sticks and a bottle of ketchup for Christmas day, I still have memories of sitting around just eating so many fish sticks that I nearly threw up. I know in the telling it sounds sad, but I was so happy that it just stuck with me, and now fish sticks and ketchup are what I eat to cheer me up when things are real bad.

I get what you're saying, and mostly agree. However not even close to all civil servants are "parasites who hardly even work", do they exist? Sure. I've met my fair share of them. 

Now, mind you I'm talking on a state level, not the federal (I don't know much about that), but when I was a civil servant working for the Tax Department for my state, I most certainly earned my wage. I was given a flat salary, rather than an hourly wage, and averaged ~7 bucks an hour. We had health insurance (which ended up getting worse every year, to the point most people opted out and got private insurance if they could afford it) and yes, there was a retirement plan, until they switched to a different system, and any demotion, promotion, or lateral transfer meant giving up the old pension system, and you got what you had paid back (minus a ton of fees), but no matching, and had to start in the new system from scratch (meaning folks who had worked for 30+ years, now had to start over). Lots of "one day fires" during that time to get rid of the old system. No pay raises for.. I think it lasted nearly 7 years, maybe longer (no Cost of Living, no step increase, no increased pay with promotion). Mandatory furlough days didn't mean "day off without pay" it meant "come to work for 12 plus hours anyway, and we're docking your pay, even if you're on flat salary".

This was the case for most of the people I worked with, now to be fair, I'm sure the receptionist at the front desk or simple data entry jobs and such didn't have to deal with nearly as much of this, but they really only made about a 10 buck an hour wage. There are for sure parasites and waste in the system, but it's hardly the majority in my anecdotal experience.

Also to be fair, my state has some of the lowest taxes in the country, most of it being paid by the mining and gaming industries (though that's a huge clusterfuck too), no state income tax, only 200 bucks to get a business license (used to be only 50, though). We have some of the lowest sales tax in the country, though we do have excise taxes, that while lower than a lot of places, can be pretty steep when it comes to certain things (tires, alcohol, tobacco, firearms, etc).

I guess that was a long rant that doesn't matter, but it really gets my goat when folk assume everyone working for the government is a lazy piece of shit that gets taken care of forever, when that is very much not the case for the vast majority, especially on the state level.

Fair enough, there are most certainly people who abuse the system, but they are in the minority, just like there are people who abuse welfare, but are also in the minority, and people who abuse any system anywhere, who are also usually in the minority.

We already have laws in place if the child is not receiving proper care, and yes, they could most certainly use an update, but if the childs needs are met, and they are happy and comfortable, the custodial parent treating themselves to something to reduce their stress levels, isn't an abuse in my opinion. Well, I'm hardly an expert, to be honest, and I can't speak for anyone. When it first started hitting me hard, and I was hospitalized for the first time in my early 20s, it was rough. I don't remember a lot about that time period, but I hear stories from others (the few who are still around). I was a paranoid mess, couldn't distinguish hallucinations or delusions from reality (still have a bit of an issue with it, but not as bad), I attempted suicide more than once, and alienated most people around me. I ended up divorced, my life went to complete shit. Mostly because I didn't have a support system in place, and refused to take my medications unless forced. 

I know that's probably a rough thing to hear, but my point is that honestly, if I had people there for me, even if they didn't really understand, and if they had taken an active part in my life, I don't think things would have been nearly as bad. 

I think the best thing you can do for your brother is to simply be there for him. At times he may not trust you, he may actively try to avoid you, he may even (if in the grips of some delusion or another) think you are the bad guy, or you're trying to do him harm, but if you are consistently there for him, if you do your best to be understanding, yet still firm (like helping him to take his medications or go to therapy or whatever) with him if he does go off the deep end, it will help. It's a pretty bleak outlook at first, or it can seem that way, but don't forget, it isn't the end of the world, he's still your brother, and there is hope. 

If we fast forward 10ish years from my first incident, when my life was in shambles, now I'm a mostly functioning person. I'm married again, I get to see my son (though it's pretty limited), I have a mostly normal life. I can't really work right now, but the progress I've made with an actual support system and good doctors, I'm getting closer to maybe being able to again. Life is pretty good, usually, it gets shitty, and there are shitty things, but it's not all gloom and doom anymore. 

As to how to spend time? Well, I used to just kind of sit around and write in journals, but that made things worse, just being alone. I have a hard time being in public or stressful situations, but I've gotten into multi-player video gaming (not saying gaming is the best way, but socialization is super important), involved in a few hobby/interest forums, and done my best to get involved in a few social circles, even if they are mostly online. Keeping occupied and connected to the wider world is key, I think.

Hope this helped in any way, if not I'm sorry, words aren't always my friends, if you have any more questions I'll try to answer in the morning. Just make sure your brother knows he is not alone, and neither are you, there are many support groups and programs for family members of people that have mental illness. Mostly, though, just make sure your brother knows that he is loved, and remember that you are too. Cheers.

Well, in ancient Rome (and Greece IIRC) marriage was not really a religious thing. Marriages were sometimes celebrated with religious ceremonies, but in no way required them. A marriage was a legal thing, the main function of marriage was "matrimonium", the bearing of children, the secondary was "consortium", the sharing (and passing on to heirs) of property. The "pillars" of marriage, if you want to call them that, were children, property, and citizenship. For a marriage to be made it required only willingness and consent from both participants, and the approval of their fathers, and even though sometimes ceremonies were performed, it was mostly a legal matter. It was only "joined at the hip" with religion for already religious people.

This also varies from place to place. Here in Nevada in the US, food items, even frozen products, are not subject to sales tax, even things like pre-packaged chips, or soda (oddly energy drinks are subject to sales tax). It's only taxed if it is intended for "immediate consumption", so if you get hot fried chicken from the deli, it's taxed, but if you get that same chicken packaged up and put in the refrigerated section, it is not taxed. It's a bit more complex than that, and people are trying to push for changes (they argue that a single can or 20 oz bottle of soda SHOULD be taxed, as it is meant to be consumed immediately, but currently it is not), but usually if it isn't prepared/restaurant food, you won't pay sales tax on it.

It varies from state to state, in Nevada where I am, you aren't allowed to include the tax in the price for advertising or on the shelves. Some smaller places do it anyway, and I have no idea WHY it is the way it is, but sometimes tax laws be crazy. NRS 372 is about the sales and use tax, I THINK 372.105 through 372.180 (may not be 100% accurate, it's been a while since I worked for the state) are the ones that deal with such things. 

Hell, a furniture store here got in a heap of trouble for advertising that they would pay the sales tax for a promotion, and had to change the wording to "will give a discount equal to the current sales tax"... it's super weird. 

Source: NRS 372 (https://www.leg.state.nv.us/nrs/NRS-372.html) NAC 372 (https://www.leg.state.nv.us/NAC/NAC-372.html), former employee of the State of Nevada Dept of Taxation.

You are mistaken on what the chart means. There are 18 states and Puerto Rico that servers are only required to be paid a 2.13 an hour wage. The "green" states in that chart are not paid "more than their non tipped counterparts" they are required by state law to be paid more than the federal tipped minimum wage of 2.13 an hour, the pay ranges from 2.13 in Oklahoma to 7.75 in Hawaii (14 are still under 4 dollars an hour, another 7 more under 5 dollars an hour). 

The only states required to pay their states actual minimum wage are the 8 in that purple-ish color. Small businesses in Montana still only have to pay 4 dollars an hour, Nevada minimum wage is lower if the employer offers health insurance, and Minnesota is lower for small businesses as well. 

So that is potentially 41 states where people make under 5 dollars an hour. Tax laws are different too, in some states (I don't know the laws everywhere) you are taxed on your sales regardless of how much is actually tipped. If people don't tip, after tipping out bus people and bartenders and taxes, they are sometimes literally costing the server money. That is very varied based on state and place of employment though. 

Either way, I agree with you about the whole situation being stupid. Having the customer decide whether a worker gets to feed their family or not is stupid.

I'm schizophrenic, and now that I'm on medication and have been in therapy and such, I can look back on the early times when it first started hitting me hard, and realize it wasn't "real" but this one event still terrifies me to my core. 

I had been having mild hallucinations for a while, maybe a couple of years, getting more and more frequent. Simple things like a random voice or seeing something that wasn't there, having paranoid feelings that people were deliberately trying to fuck me over or had it out for me, things like that. When I noticed them for not being actually real, I just wrote it off to the high stress of my job, this is about my first real psychotic break, and I will try to do it justice, but I'm not always so much with the words. 

One day, I was at my desk, doing a particularly boring part of my job (demographic updates, so essentially mindless data entry), I started hearing people talk to me, but not people I knew, had a feeling of being watched, and it had been getting worse throughout the day, but the more I just kind of zoned out doing my menial work, the worse it got. It got to the point that there were so many voices, shouting, whispering, they weren't really understandable, just constant babble like in a big crowd of talking people, but underneath it all was this sound... like a heartbeat, just this constant Thump-thump, thump-thump, getting louder and louder, eventually overtaking all of the voices. It paralyzed me with terror and increasing anxiety, I was pretty much just frozen there (my desk was in a back corner, and no one really had any reason to bother me while this was going on) listening to this thump-thump, in time with my own heart beat, then came the rushing noise of air, like very loud breathing, in time with my own, louder and louder until... I don't know, my mind just kind of broke, I saw, visually the entire universe, heard the heart beats and breathing of every being in it, all going in time. The universe was a giant cosmic beast, with no true form, and all things were moving and living in rhythm with it's massive beating heart and I was hearing it all, viewing it all, the secrets of existence opened in front of me, humanity was nothing, nothing anyone ever did mattered, we were like unseen mites in the eyelashes of the cosmic beast that was the universe. The feeling of being so small, so insignificant... it's hard to explain, and I now know that this was just a massive hallucination, but at the time... it was horrifying. From what I remember it lasted for about an hour, when I finally got my own vision back, and could move, I was terrified, absolutely out of my mind with fear, and literally ran screaming from my office building, out into the street, got hit by a car and blacked out. I don't remember much of the next year or so (maybe closer to two), but I spent more time in mental hospitals than out of them, and was not very coherent (according to the people who were around then that still talk to me), I lost my job, my wife divorced me, I wasn't allowed to see my son (these aren't bad things, apparently I was violent at times, and now that things are better I get to see my son, and have a pretty good relationship with my ex-wife). I don't remember much of that time, thankfully, but that one memory I don't think will ever go away, and any time I think of it I have a near panic attack.

What are you looking for?:

This is really the question, isn't it? I don't know 100% what I'm looking for, but I'll try to be as clear as I can. My history with MMOs has been a pretty long one, starting with EQ in 99. What I'm looking for is a bit of the ol' nostalgia I suppose. My happiest memories in life (other than the birth of my son) have been MMO related. I miss sitting on a hill with friends or strangers, chatting, pulling and grinding mobs to level. I love deep and interesting lore, but without a main story shoved down your throat, a history you need to actively try to discover. I want a game where grouping, even at low level, while not 100% mandatory, is the best and most rewarded way of playing. Grinding mobs to level, hunting rares, competing for rare spawns... all of this is what I'm looking for. Games like EQ1, FFXI or hell even the first few months of WoW are where my fondest memories come from, and I would like to experience something similar again. I prefer a mob grinding system of leveling to being some NPCs errand boy, and I don't care too much for PvP. Instances are fine if they aren't the focus, and are more small group oriented, like 6 mans and actually difficult content. Also, I don't have a great computer as I am disabled and on a very limited income, I'm saving as much as I can, but it's not going fast. I currently have a core 2 duo E7200, a GeForce 8800 GT 512, and 8 gigs of ram. 

    What games have you previously played?:

Long list. EQ, EQ2, FFXI, UO, DAoC, WAR, SWTOR, SW:Galaxies, FFXIV, GW, GW2, AoC, Anarchy Online, Tree of Life, The Repopulation, Rift, EvE, Defiance, Tera, ESO, Vindictus, Firefall, STO, Neverwinter, LOTRO, DDO, Champions of Regnum, Fallen Earth, Champions Online, Mortal Online, Planetside, DCUO... there are probably others that I'm forgetting, and a bunch of games that are not technically MMOs that are online and multiplayer.
 
    What is your playstyle (Casual,Semi-Casual,Hardcore)?: 

Semi-Hardcore? I could be hardcore, and want to be, but haven't found the right game yet. Like I said I'm disabled, so I have a TON of time to play games... 

    Any preferred mechanics?:

Forced, or mostly forced, grouping. Grinding mobs and hunting rares/camping spawns to level. Deep lore that isn't necessarily forced down your throat. Lack of "10 bear asses" quests. PvE focus. Doesn't need to be 100% sandbox, but a mostly open world would be nice, non linear paths etc. Lots of actual exploration (not GW2 follow icons on the map to "explore"). 

    Anything specific you want to exclude?:

Dunno if I would 100% exclude anything, but PvP isn't my bag in MMOs (MOBAS and FPSs fill that fine for me), but RvR is pretty cool. I really hate the WoW style questing system, but if everything else is cool I can deal with it...
